name: Nullbreak
description: Nullbreak is an aggressive neurochemical intervention that physically disrupts established dependency pathways using targeted SNT-mediated synaptic pruning, forcing the brain to rebuild reward circuits from a clean baseline. The process is intensely painful — users describe three to five days of psychological and physical agony — but the result is a near-complete severance of chemical dependency for a broad spectrum of substances. Not for the faint of will.
effects: Complete dependency pathway severance (72-120 hour process)
Eliminates physical addiction substrate for target substance
Reduced relapse risk at 6-month follow-up compared to gradual methods
side_effects: Extreme pain during process (rated 8-10/10 by most users)
Approximately 8% of users develop new compulsive behaviors as replacement pathways form
Rare: permanent alteration of reward sensitivity
cultural_context: Nullbreak is what you do when you're serious. In Tier 3 and 4, it's offered by licensed detox facilities with supervision suites — patients are monitored through the worst of it. On the street, rumors circulate of unlicensed Nullbreak 'sweat lodges' in the Shelf where addicts go through it together with nothing but water and each other. The survival rate in those settings is not good.
story_hooks: A fixer needs to be clean for a critical job in 10 days — Nullbreak is the only option, but she has no access to a supervised facility and will have to go through it alone
A Helix researcher is quietly investigating why a small percentage of Nullbreak patients emerge with entirely different compulsive patterns — patterns that seem almost useful
Someone discovers the Shelf sweat lodge operation and has to decide whether to shut it down or protect it — it's the only real detox option for people who can't afford clinics
